en.title: Silent Night, Holy Night
en.author: Joseph Mohr
stanzas:
[A]Silent night, holy night,
[E7]All is calm, [A]all is bright
[D]Round yon virgin mother and [A]Child.
[D]Holy Infant, so [A]tender and mild,
[E7]Sleep in heavenly [A]peace,
Sleep in heaven[E7]ly [A]peace.

Silent night, holy night,
Shepherds quake at the sight;
Glories stream from heaven afar,
Heavenly hosts sing Alleluia!
Christ the Savior is born,
Christ the Savior is born!

Silent night, holy night,
Son of God, love's pure light;
Radiant beams from Thy holy face
With the dawn of redeeming grace,
Jesus, Lord, at Thy birth,
Jesus, Lord, at Thy birth.

de.title: Stille Nacht, heilige Nacht
de.author: Joseph Mohr
stanzas:
[A]Stille Nacht, heilige Nacht!
[E7]Alles schläft, [A]einsam wacht
[D]nur das traute, hochheilige [A]Paar.
[D]Holder Knabe im [A]lockigen Haar,
[E7]schlaf in himmlischer [A]Ruh,
schlaf in himmli[E7]scher [A]Ruh.

Stille Nacht, heilige Nacht!
Hirten erst kundgemacht,
durch der Engel Halleluja
tönt es laut von fern und nah:
Christ, der Retter, ist da,
Christ, der Retter, ist da!

Stille Nacht, heilige Nacht!
Gottes Sohn, o wie lacht
Lieb aus deinem göttlichen Mund,
da uns schlägt die rettende Stund,
Christ, in deiner Geburt,
Christ, in deiner Geburt.

notes: German: the 'gebräuchliche Fassung' — the three sung stanzas as cited on de.wikipedia from Evangelisches Gesangbuch (Bayern/Thüringen, 2. Aufl. München 1995, S. 101), in the modern printed order (Mohr's original stanzas 1, 6, 2). Mohr's full six-stanza autograph text of 1816 is on de.wikisource (Weyhnachts-Lied, and Gruber's Autograph VII) and reads 'Jesus' where the EG has 'Christ', 'lockigten' for 'lockigen' and 'Hirten erst kundgemacht ... bei Ferne und Nah'; those older forms are deliberately not used here per the EG-orthography rule. English: the Cyber Hymnal's four stanzas — stanzas 1 and 3 are John Freeman Young's 1863 translation, stanzas 2 and 4 are anonymous, and hymnary confirms that split; stanza 4 is the least commonly printed. Hymnary's representative English text also shows a widely printed variant of stanza 2 beginning 'Darkness flies, all is light'. Meter is hymnary's tune-page value; its text page says only 'Irregular'. Tune STILLE NACHT (Gruber, 1818) is printed in B-flat; A is the nearest preferred guitar key (one semitone down) and the two texts' charts agree bar for bar. Cross-checked 2026-08-02: English against Timeless Truths (independent; agrees word for word, variants case/punctuation only — 'holy night!', capital 'King' in st. 4 where the Cyber Hymnal source prints lowercase 'king', kept here); German against evangeliums.net (independent; identical wording, though it capitalizes 'Deinem/Deiner' where the EG style kept here has lowercase).
